== Biography ==
The profile retains an uncertain birth bound before 2 February 1777 and its inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire locality. A separate Livingston baptism transcript dated 2 February 1777 names Janet Glasgow and parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; it remains a compatible candidate, not a resolved identity. The retained assessment treats [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] as possible father (43%) and leaves [[Davidson-14073|Christine Davidson]] unrated as mother. An earlier draft estimated a birth about 1780 and stated the parentage more firmly; both are superseded draft claims, not current conclusions.

=== Livingston monument comparison, 24 October 2026 ===

Two Findmypast derivatives of a Livingston family monument name a daughter Janet of Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; one indexes Janet's death as 16 October 1853 aged 76, compatible with the separate 2 February 1777 baptism, while the other reads 16 October 1873 aged 76, which is not compatible with that baptism. The fuller derivative calls the erector “Janet Glasgow, Blackburn”; Blackburn may be a locality after the name and does not prove a married surname. The public BillionGraves index describes the same family but its photograph preview is too blurred to read, and its own dates cannot settle these disagreements.<ref name="LivingstonMI2026">Findmypast, Scotland Monumental Inscriptions, Livingston, derivative transcriptions [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00422894&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00422894] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511321&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511321] (captured 24 October 2026); compare [https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 BillionGraves, Thomas Glasgow, marker LV 106], public index checked 24 October 2026. The BillionGraves photo preview is blurred and the original inscription was not independently read. The three derivative accounts conflict on years, ages and some dates; they are not three independent witnesses to a precise vital fact.</ref>

[[Glasgow-1448]] remains a strengthened compatible candidate for the record-defined Janet. Her inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire birth-place claim and Blackburn surname basis remain unverified; no monumental death or birth-place change is assigned. The existing 43% possible father assessment and unassessed mother status are retained pending an original inscription, her marriage/death records, and the Bridgeton claim's source.
